summary: Registering an OAuth application with Beeminder is an instant, self-serve process requiring only an application name and a redirect URL. The primary consideration is ensuring API calls use canonical HTTPS URLs and exact redirect URI matching to prevent dropped parameters.

difficulty.headline: Beeminder provides immediate, self-serve OAuth app registration without requiring manual review or developer approval.

factors.label: Self-Serve Instant Access
factors.detail: OAuth applications can be registered instantly on the web without any developer application wait time or manual approval process.

factors.label: Minimal App Requirements
factors.detail: Creating an application only requires providing an Application Name and a Redirect URL.

evidence.quote: Application name and redirect URL are required.

factors.label: Strict Redirect URI Matching
factors.detail: Authorization requests fail if the redirect_uri parameter does not exactly match the registered redirect URL.

evidence.quote: This must match the redirect URL you supplied when you registered your app above.

can_test_before_approval.detail: Developers can register an app instantly at beeminder.com/apps/new and test OAuth authorization and API endpoints immediately without waiting for review or approval.

requirements.label: Beeminder User Account
requirements.detail: An active account on Beeminder is required to register and manage OAuth apps.

requirements.label: Application Name
requirements.detail: A unique identifier name for the OAuth application.

evidence.quote: Application name and redirect URL are required.

requirements.label: Redirect URL
requirements.detail: The callback URL where users will be sent with their access_token and username upon authorizing the app.

evidence.quote: The redirect URL is where the user is sent after authorizing your app.

steps.title: Log into your Beeminder account
steps.detail: Sign in to your account on Beeminder to access developer settings and application registration.

steps.title: Prepare application settings and redirect URI
steps.detail: Determine the application name and exact callback URI to handle the OAuth authentication redirect.
steps.agent_assist: Draft the application name and prepare the exact callback URL structure (e.g., https://yourdomain.com/auth/beeminder/callback) for registration.

evidence.quote: Application name and redirect URL are required.

steps.title: Register the app on Beeminder
steps.detail: Navigate to the app registration page at beeminder.com/apps/new, fill in your app name and redirect URL, and submit.
steps.agent_assist: Provide exact application parameters to paste into the form fields at beeminder.com/apps/new.

steps.title: Retrieve client_id from registered apps list
steps.detail: Access beeminder.com/apps to retrieve your application's client_id for use in authorization requests.
steps.agent_assist: Prepare application configuration files or environment variable templates to store the client_id securely.

steps.title: Construct authorization URL for user authentication
steps.detail: Build the OAuth authorization endpoint URL containing client_id, URL-encoded redirect_uri, and response_type set to token.
steps.agent_assist: Generate authorization request URL formatted as https://www.beeminder.com/apps/authorize?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=token.

evidence.quote: The base URL is the same for all apps: https://www.beeminder.com/apps/authorize.

steps.title: Receive and store user access tokens
steps.detail: Implement server or client handling to extract access_token and username from query parameters when Beeminder redirects the user back.
steps.agent_assist: Draft authorization callback code to parse GET query parameters access_token and username and associate them with your user's account.

evidence.quote: After the user authorizes your application they'll be redirected to the redirect_uri that you specified, with two additional parameters, access_token and username, in the query string.

gotchas.title: POST Parameters Stripped on HTTP or Missing-www Requests
gotchas.detail: Beeminder redirects HTTP or non-www requests to canonical HTTPS URLs, but strips POST parameters during the redirect, causing opaque API failures.

evidence.quote: We redirect insecure and non www requests to the canonical Beeminder URL, but do not forward parameters for POST requests

gotchas.title: Redirect URI Mismatch
gotchas.detail: The redirect_uri query parameter in authorization requests must be URL-encoded and match the exact string registered in your app settings.

evidence.quote: This must match the redirect URL you supplied when you registered your app above.

gotchas.title: Incorrect Canonical API Base URL
gotchas.detail: All API endpoints require the full canonical HTTPS base URL with the www subdomain included.

evidence.quote: The base URL for all requests is https://www.beeminder.com/api/v1/.

blockers.problem: POST requests to Beeminder fail silently or return error responses
blockers.why: Using insecure HTTP or omitting the www subdomain triggers a 301/302 redirect that drops request parameters.
blockers.fix: Ensure all API requests explicitly target https://www.beeminder.com/api/v1/ as the base URL.

evidence.quote: We redirect insecure and non www requests to the canonical Beeminder URL, but do not forward parameters for POST requests

blockers.problem: Users encounter an error when redirected to Beeminder's authorization screen
blockers.why: The redirect_uri provided in the authorization request does not match the URI registered at beeminder.com/apps/new.
blockers.fix: Verify that special characters in redirect_uri are percent-encoded and match the registered app redirect URL exactly.

evidence.quote: This must match the redirect URL you supplied when you registered your app above.

blockers.problem: Compromised personal auth token during local development
blockers.why: A personal authentication token was checked into source control or exposed publicly.
blockers.fix: Regenerate the token immediately via Account Settings > Apps & API to invalidate the compromised token.

uncertain: Official rate limits for API requests are not stated in the documentation.
Access token expiration timelines and refresh token mechanisms are not specified.
